tagline: A watch kept on the world — live air traffic, weather, markets, space weather, seismic and volcanic activity, satellites, and conflict, pulled live into one screen.
caps: every aircraft in the sky, live
launchSub: Encrypted behind a login · public feeds only · runs in your browser, with a small relay for the feeds a browser can't read

cards.html: Vanilla JS pulling directly from public sources — Open-Meteo, CoinGecko, Frankfurter, NOAA, USGS, NASA, weather.gov, wheretheiss.at, GDELT. The few that a browser isn't allowed to read (OpenSky and the ADS-B receiver networks, GDELT's event files, NOAA's large solar-wind files) go through a small owner-only relay on mentifaber.org that trims and briefly caches them and stores nothing else.

features.d: every aircraft broadcasting a position worldwide, moving smoothly on its own map and the globe — tap one for its route, photo and live numbers, find any flight by callsign, and watch for emergency squawks and military traffic.
current conditions and active NWS severe weather alerts.
NOAA's R/S/G storm scales, solar wind and magnetic field with 24-hour charts, X-ray flares, the 3-day Kp forecast, and NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day.
USGS earthquake and volcanic activity, elevated-status alerts included.
live ISS position and satellite ground tracks.
violence reported in world news over the last two hours, read from GDELT's 15-minute event stream and mapped by place.

lede: The information that actually matters day to day — is a storm coming, did the market move, is anything seismic or volcanic worth paying attention to, where's the ISS, what's happening globally — lives scattered across a dozen different sites and apps. Vigil is a single personal dashboard that pulls the live, public feeds worth checking into one place.
scope: This is a personal dashboard, not an early-warning system — treat every feed as informational, not authoritative, and go to the source (NWS, USGS, NOAA directly) for anything that actually matters in the moment. The dashboard itself is encrypted (AES-256, key derived from the operator name and access code) — without them the page is unreadable ciphertext, even in the source.
closing: A watch kept on the world, one feed at a time.
